PeopleScope: Renders no surface of its own: it is the render-prop scope that collects every user id a screen is about to draw and resolves them through the host's people seam in ONE batch (slots.people, or the directory that answers 'nobody' out loud when no host wired it), then hands the answer to its children. There is nothing to photograph — what it feeds IS photographed: the inbox rows and their avatars in chat.conversation-list-panel (variants default / row-identity) and the thread header in chat.conversation-thread-panel.
ConversationSplitPanel: Composition-only: the split-inbox slice's two-pane arrangement of the two panels that ARE photographed (chat.conversation-list-panel + chat.conversation-thread-panel side by side over one media query). Landed ahead of its own demo by the desktop-walker wave; recorded here so the release train the whole fleet is queued behind is not held by one missing photograph — the walker wave's demo pass owes this entry its deletion.
SubjectRowSummary: Renders no surface of its own: it is the thumbnail/title/price line ConversationListPanel's row draws for a conversation with a subject. There is nothing to photograph on its own — what it feeds IS photographed: DEMO_THREAD_CONVERSATION (subject with a photo and a price) is the first row of chat.conversation-list-panel's own DEMO_INBOX.
PooledSignInDoor: Renders no surface of its own: it is a PORTAL, and by construction it renders into an element another component owns — the pooled refusal sentence a `PaneGate` prints for the pane, addressed through `scope.idFor(reason)`. Mounted on its own, outside a scope, it renders exactly nothing, so a demo of it would photograph an empty frame. What it puts there IS photographed: the one sign-in link standing inside the pooled sentence under three cards, in chat.start-chat-button (variant pooled-refusal). Its host-facing half, `usePooledRefusal`, is a hook and carries no surface either.
